sentences[0].whyEn: Past perfect in the clause → nachdem: first the meal, then going out.
sentences[1].whyEn: The before: bevor — verb at the end.
sentences[2].whyEn: Simultaneous: während — two things at the same time.
sentences[3].whyEn: From the start until now: seit(dem) — with the present tense.
sentences[4].whyEn: Up to the end point: bis.
sentences[9].whyEn: seit + present tense, verb last: wohne.
sentences[11].whyEn: Simultaneous in the past: während (or als).
sentences[12].whyEn: Until the end point: bis du fertig bist.
sentences[13].whyEn: beendet hatte — be- without ge-, hatte last.
sentences[14].whyEn: seit + present: habe — the state continues.
sentences[15].whyEn: Right after: sobald du zu Hause bist.
sentences[17].whyEn: seit + present: ist — the retirement is ongoing.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Before the film started, we bought popcorn.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: While I was working, the phone rang.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: nachdem marks the earlier event and takes the Plusquamperfekt (gegessen hatten); bevor and während keep the main clause's tense.
help.tips[0].en.text: Nachdem wir gegessen hatten, gingen wir. Bevor ich gehe, rufe ich an. Warte, bis ich komme. Während sie kocht, deckt er den Tisch. All with the verb at the end.
help.tips[0].en.title: nachdem = earlier (Plusquamperfekt); bevor / bis = later; während = same time
help.tips[0].en.trap: 'before' tempts a tense shift ('before I had gone'); German bevor takes the plain tense of the main clause. Only nachdem goes one step back.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Since she's been ill, she hasn't come to sport any more.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Since I have lived in Hamburg, I have cycled every day.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: seit for something that started in the past and still continues takes the present tense in German.
help.tips[1].en.text: Seit ich hier wohne, habe ich kein Auto. (English: since I've lived here, I've had …) The German present covers what began in the past and continues. seitdem is the fuller form, same meaning.
help.tips[1].en.title: seit(dem) + present tense
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: When I arrived it was dark. When I arrive I'll call.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: As soon as the bus comes, we will set off.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: One single period in the past is als. wenn is for repeated, present or future events, and wann is a question word.
help.tips[2].en.text: als = once in the past (Als ich Kind war). wenn = repeated, present or future (Wenn es regnet; Wenn ich fertig bin, rufe ich an). sobald = as soon as (Sobald der Bus kommt, fahren wir los) — a stronger wenn.
help.tips[2].en.title: als vs wenn, and sobald
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: After the meal we went out. = After we had eaten, we went out.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: nachdem's preposition twin is nach (+ Dativ): nach dem Essen.
help.tips[3].en.text: nachdem ↔ nach, bevor ↔ vor, während ↔ während (+Gen), seit(dem) ↔ seit (+Dat), bis ↔ bis. Nach dem Essen = Nachdem wir gegessen hatten. The twin comes into play later in the course.
help.tips[3].en.title: Each conjunction has a preposition twin
help.context.en: Since I've lived in Hamburg, I cycle every day. Before I set off, I look at the weather app. While I ride, I listen to podcasts. After I've arrived at the office, I have a quick shower. And as soon as the working day ends, I ride to the Elbe – until it gets dark.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: seit takes the present for a continuing state.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: bevor takes the same tense as the main clause.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: A single past period is als.
help.mistakes[3].whyEn: nachdem with a past main clause needs the Plusquamperfekt in its own clause (hatte / war + participle).
help.hookEn: Put events in order — before, after, while, since, until — and your stories stop being a flat list of sentences.
help.introEn: Temporal clauses fix the order of events, and German has one conjunction per relation, each sending its verb to the end. Earlier: nachdem (after — with the Plusquamperfekt) and als / wenn (when — one past event / repeated or future). Same time: während (while). Later: bevor (before), bis (until). Start point: seit / seitdem (since — present tense in German where English uses the perfect: Seit ich hier wohne, habe ich kein Auto). Trigger: sobald (as soon as). Every one of these has a preposition twin for use with a noun — nach dem Essen, vor dem Film, während der Arbeit, seit zwei Jahren, bis Montag — and choosing clause or noun phrase comes later in the course; for now, the clauses. Note bevor and während take the same tense as the main clause; only nachdem shifts back. The quiz tests both decisions: which conjunction fits, and which tense follows it — Plusquamperfekt after nachdem, the present after seit, the same tense as the main clause after bevor.
help.rememberEn[0]: nachdem → Plusquamperfekt; bevor, während, bis, sobald → same tense; seit → present.
